name: Jamsocket

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

caveats: Discontinued: acquired by Modal (2025-07-10); hosted platform terminated 2026-03-04 (signups closed since 2026-01-08). Successor = Modal Sandboxes (card 'modal'); Plane and Y-Sweet remain as MIT open-source self-host projects with little planned development.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Nested virtualization set to no: every sandbox runs under gVisor, which gives the workload its own user-space kernel and no /dev/kvm device (no KVM-based emulators or VMs inside). Docker inside is a separate question.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When a sandbox is idle, its memory is snapshotted before it is “detached” from the worker.
snapshot_auto.note: HISTORICAL, ForeverVM product only (discontinued; forevervm.com now redirects to modal.com). Trigger: idle; memory (Python REPL state) included; resumed transparently on next instruction. The Jamsocket session-backend platform itself had no snapshots: backends were terminated after max_idle_seconds/lifetime_limit_seconds and persisting state was the app's job (blob storage/DB).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Session backends are useful for maintaining document state while a user session is active, but they require a way to store that data when a session has ended.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Neither the full Jamsocket HTTP API v2 (connect/status/logs/metrics/terminate/services/images) nor the ForeverVM API (create/list machines, exec) had a snapshot/checkpoint/fork endpoint. Historical: service terminated 2026-03-04.

harness_api.quote: Currently Jamsocket will only allow HTTP requests and Sockets connections to be proxied to the backend.
harness_api.note: WebSocket session-backend platform (spawn your own Docker image); ForeverVM exposed a Python REPL exec API plus an MCP server, not a harness-driving API.

ingress_rules.quote: This Connection URL comes with a secret token. Treat the connection token like a bearer token, because any client that knows it can access the backend.
ingress_rules.note: Tokenized per-backend URLs (requests without the token rejected); only port 8080 proxied, HTTP/WebSocket only; optional secret_token and unforgeable x-verified-* user headers. Historical.

secret_proxy.quote: Spawn a session backend with env vars that include what bucket to access and credentials to access it with.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets passed as env vars in the spawn request (executable.env); no injecting proxy documented.
